threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you're new when you still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line'. The locals have their own lingo down here.
Caught a guy on the N133 last night singing opera to a bemused group of night revellers. Must've been a forgotten star—missed my stop listening.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a lady negotiating with a pigeon over a bread roll at Tempelhofer Feld while the sun set. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous techno raves in the forest at night. Just follow the sound—nature meets the Berliner party spirit. It's surreal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART on Fridays—too many overheated brakes and smoke alarms to make it worth it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy bring his pet iguana on the 38 today, and the driver just shrugged. Only in San Francisco, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí; they miss the tiny, winding streets where neighbors still gather for xurreria at all hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones baffled by the schedule of the Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat, staring at the screens like they’re reading hieroglyphics.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still using a plastic umbrella; locals know a proper Hackney day demands a sturdy one, or you'll be left wet and sorry.
Last night on the 77, a guy sat beside me singing elevator music to himself. Honestly, it was oddly calming amid the chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the spontaneous street party outside my window turned into an impromptu dance-off, and I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 4 AM and then stumble into a techno party in a backroom café where the vibe's somehow both chaotic and cozy.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know to avoid the BART station when it’s foggy; the tourists always think it's just a light drizzle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy practicing stand-up on the 19 Polk. Front row was a packed crowd, he had them laughing about the Muni delays. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think tapas are a snack, but for us, it’s a whole evening ritual—pa amb tomàquet and vermut, without a rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still use the 'V' in 'Barcelona' instead of just 'Barna' when chatting with locals.
